# The Choir
[italic]If you are reading this page alone, stop. Find someone. Read it together.[/italic]
Most people who go deep into the [textlink="Unmooring" link="WFLoreUnmooring"] come back frightened. A few come back calm. They hum while they work. They ask to be put on the long hauls. They stop sleeping in their bunks and start sleeping by the viewports, facing out.
They are the [color=#d070ff]Choir[/color], and they say they heard [textlink="the Monolith's" link="WFLoreMonolith"] song out past the anchors. They say it was the most beautiful thing they have ever heard. They say it knew their names.
## What they want
Nobody has ever got a straight answer. What they do is plain enough:
- They keep the black stones. Dark hulls drift in the deep with a Scion bolted to the deck and robed figures minding it, and a ship standing off that hails once and then opens fire. - They break [textlink="anchors" link="WFLoreLattice"]. Every relay that goes dark, every breach, the song gets a little closer. - They carry the stones inward, to people who would never go out to meet one.
## How it starts
Nobody is taken. That is the worst of it. The song only reaches those already far into Drift, and only those who answer it are Choir. The rest hear something, once, and are never quite sure afterwards that they didn't.
[italic]Interview, deck hand, name withheld, after a hauler came back short two crew.[/italic]
"It wasn't like a voice. It was like remembering a song you didn't know you knew. And there was a part where you're supposed to join in. I could feel where it was. I didn't. I don't know why I didn't."
"Do you know why the other two did?"
"I think they were braver than me."
## Signs
Humming, in a key that doesn't fit the tune. A crewman who stops looking at the stars and starts looking past them. A Remade that walks past someone and does not turn.
[italic]If you recognise the tune, close this book.[/italic]
